Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: We've noticed he tends to sit very close to the TV when watching cartoons or leans in really close when looking at pictures in his books. It's almost as if he can't see them clearly from a normal distance.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: There are times when we call his name and he doesn't respond right away. It's not all the time, but often enough that we wonder if he's having trouble hearing us.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Lately, he's been complaing about tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods like ice cream or cold yogurt. This started a few months ago and has been consistent since then.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist found a structural abnormality in his heart. We go for regular check-ups to monitor it and make sure it doesn't affect his daily life too much.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He was born with a tethered cord. The doctors said this could potentially affect his development and we're keeping a close eye on how he progresses.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Compared to his peers, our son gains weight slowly. He eats well and doesn't show signs of discomfort after eating but just doesn't seem to put on weight as quickly as other kids his age.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Our child has scoliosis. We're working with physical therapy to help improve his posture and reduce the curvature of his spine.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary enlargement of the tonsils (tonsillitis).

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Our child has a structural abnormality in his heart, specifically tethered cord syndrome, which requires ongoing monitoring.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Approximately 11% of children with KBG syndrome develop tethered cord syndrome, characterized by an abnormally positioned spinal cord that can lead to various neurological complications.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Our child experiences feeding difficulties and slow weight gain compared to peers.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may exhibit feeding difficulties, slow weight gain, and difficulty gaining weight despite adequate caloric intake.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Our child has tethered cord syndrome, requiring ongoing monitoring for potential neurological complications.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Approximately 11% of children with KBG syndrome develop tethered cord syndrome, characterized by an abnormally positioned spinal cord that can lead to various neurological complications.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Our child experiences ear infections and a tendency to lean closer to the television while watching.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary enlargement of the tonsils (tonsillitis).

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Our child experiences sensitivity to cold temperatures in his teeth upon consuming cold food items.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience dental issues, such as weak enamel and sensitivity to cold temperatures, particularly in the molars.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Our child experiences sensitivity to cold temperatures in his molars upon consuming cold food items.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience dental issues, such as weak enamel and sensitivity to cold temperatures, particularly in the molars.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Our child attends a mainstream primary school but requires additional support and accommodations due to his cognitive delays and behavioral differences.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may require additional educational support, such as Individual Education Plans (IEPs) or Special Educational Needs (SEN) plans, to address their unique needs.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Our child exhibits behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences are common in individuals with KBG syndrome and may impact social interactions, emotional regulation, and academic performance.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Our child has brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger) due to the structural anomaly in his heart.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome may have variations in their skeletal structures, such as short fingers (brachydactyly) and a curvature of the fifth finger (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS

a) Recommendations for screening and treatments:
- Regular dental check-ups: Monitoring for dental issues, especially concerning molars.
- Regular hearing reviews: Age 5 and beyond to ensure proper hearing acuity.
- Orthopedic review: Considering a review for tethered cord syndrome, given the potential for neurological complications.
- Cardiologist follow-up: Continued monitoring of heart-related concerns, including echocardiograms and ECGs.
- Neurological evaluation: Periodic review for tethered cord syndrome, considering the risk of neurological complications.
- Speech therapy: Addressing communication and swallowing challenges.
- Behavioural therapy: Supporting social and emotional development.
- Physical therapy: Promoting overall strength and flexibility.
- Occupational therapy: Enhancing fine motor skills and daily living abilities.
- Dietitian consultation: Addressing feeding difficulties and ensuring adequate nutrition.
- Genetic counseling: Discussing the possibility of future pregnancies with a genetic counselor.

### Recommendations for Screening and Treatments

#### Vision
- Regular eye checks recommended, particularly for children with KBG syndrome. Monitoring for refractive errors and potential vision-related issues such as strabismus or astigmatism.

#### Hearing
- Audiometric screening should be conducted annually starting from early childhood. Addressing hearing concerns promptly, especially concerning conductive hearing loss associated with adenovirus infections.

#### Teeth
- Frequent dental visits recommended, considering the high prevalence of dental issues. Orthodontic evaluation may be warranted given the risk of craniofacial anomalies.

#### Heart
- Follow-up echocardiography and ECG monitoring post-diagnosis. Consider referral for cardiac review if concerns arise regarding heart valve abnormalities or previous murmurs.

#### Tethered Cord
- MRI review considered if sacral dimple is noted or if there are concerns about sacral alignment or asymmetry. Management options include observation, physical therapy, or surgical intervention.

#### Palate
- Review and consideration of referral for palate assessment if feeding difficulties persist or if there are concerns about speech development or feeding tolerance.

#### Neurological
- Regular neurological assessments recommended to monitor for potential developmental delays or behavioral differences. Early identification and management of cognitive and behavioral challenges can improve outcomes.

#### Immunology
- Routine immunizations should be administered according to standard protocols. Consideration of additional vaccinations based on individual risk factors and clinical judgment.

#### GI System
- Dietary restrictions and food preferences should be addressed with pediatric dietitians or nutritionists familiar with KBG syndrome. Feeding strategies and timing should be discussed with healthcare providers experienced in managing this condition.

#### Behaviour and Development
- Behavioral interventions and therapies should be considered if developmental milestones are consistently delayed or if behavioral differences are observed. Evidence-based approaches tailored to the individual child should be implemented.

#### Skeletal
- Regular skeletal surveys (e.g., wrist X-rays) should be performed to assess bone age and detect potential growth plate issues. Monitoring for signs of skeletal anomalies, such as brachydactyly and clinodactyly, should be ongoing.

#### Education
- Individualized Education Programmes (IEPs) should be developed and reviewed periodically to address academic needs. Collaboration between educators, therapists, and healthcare professionals is essential for optimal educational planning.

#### Medical Concerns
- Regular review of growth parameters and hormonal status should be undertaken to monitor for potential deficiencies or imbalances. Consideration of thyroid function testing and other relevant laboratory evaluations may be warranted.

- Encourage parental involvement in educational settings to support understanding of the child’s unique needs and accommodations required for successful integration into mainstream environments.
- Consider psychological support for the child and family, particularly if behavioral differences or developmental delays impact emotional wellbeing. Consulting with a psychologist or child behavior specialist can provide valuable insights and resources.

- Given the variability in the severity of ANKRD11-related syndromes, close monitoring of key features is crucial. Regular follow-up appointments with specialists should be scheduled to address emerging concerns and track progression over time.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent respiratory infections requiring antibiotic treatment.
- Occasional episodes of bronchiectasis-like presentation.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Rare occurrence of bronchiectasis in KBG syndrome patients.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- No congenital heart defects were noted.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Congenital heart defects are a known complication in KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)-related symptoms.
- Occasional episodes of eosinophilic esophagitis.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- GERD is a recognized feature in KBG syndrome patients.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent viral and bacterial infections requiring immunotherapy.
- Increased risk of autoimmune reactions.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Increased susceptibility to autoimmune diseases in KBG syndrome patients.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent seizures requiring anticonvulsant medications.
- Neurodevelopmental delays and behavioral differences.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Neurodevelopmental delays and behavioral differences are a known feature in KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent ear infections leading to prolonged hospital stays.
- Nasal congestion and sinusitis.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Ear infections are a common feature in KBG syndrome patients.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent vision-related issues such as astigmatism and refractive errors.
- Glue ear (otosome) requiring frequent audiologic evaluations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision-related issues are a recognized feature in KBG syndrome patients.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent skin complaints such as eczema and keratosis pilaris.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skin complaints are a recognized feature in KBG syndrome patients.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent tooth decay requiring dental interventions.
- Orthodontic considerations due to brachydactyly.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Tooth decay is a recognized feature in KBG syndrome patients.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Requires additional educational support and accommodations.
- May require transition to a more specialized educational setting.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Additional educational support is recommended for all children with KBG syndrome.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) traits.
- Learning difficulties and cognitive delays.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences and learning difficulties are recognized features in KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved 5th finger).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal anomalies are a recognized feature in KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
### Screening Recommendations:
- Regular dental check-ups.
- Monitoring for glue ear (otosome) and sensorineural hearing loss.
- Periodic cardiovascular assessments (e.g., echocardiogram, ECG).

### Treatments Recommendations:
- Antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) for seizure management.
- Immunotherapy (e.g., intravenous immunoglobulin, corticosteroids) for recurrent infections.
- Speech therapy and occupational therapy for developmental delays and communication challenges.
- Physical therapy for maintaining joint flexibility and preventing contractures.
- Nutritional counseling for managing feeding difficulties and potential GI issues.
- Epilepsy management plan (e.g., AED dosing schedule, seizure frequency tracking).

This comprehensive approach addresses the unique medical needs of KBG syndrome patients while providing guidance on how these requirements impact broader aspects of their lives.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has a bit of a problem with her eyes, specifically she has hypermetropia, which means she has trouble seeing things up close. She holds books really close to her face to read.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes she asks us to repeat ourselves because she didn't quite catch what we said the first time. It's like she needs a little extra help to understand.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth are a concern; the dentist mentioned that the enamel is weak. We're working on making sure she brushes them gently and regularly.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Physically, she can't keep going for very long without getting tired. Simple games like tag or running around exhaust her quicker than her friends.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Now and then, she'll just stare off into space for a few seconds. It's unnerving at first, but it happens often enough that we've learned to recognize it and make sure she's okay afterward.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food wise, she's extremely picky about textures. Some foods she just won't touch if they have the wrong feel. Mealtime can be challenging because of this.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Two other things - her fontanelle took longer than usual to close, and there are these palatal abnormalities we're keeping an eye on. The specialists are monitoring both closely.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and potential for chronic sinusitis. Proper hygiene practices and timely antibiotic treatment can help prevent or reduce the frequency of these infections.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, specifically a hole in the heart (septal defect). Monitoring and follow-up with a cardiologist are recommended to ensure proper management and address any concerns regarding the heart.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and swallowing challenges. These issues can lead to poor weight gain and delayed milestones. Management strategies such as tube feeding, dietary modifications, and therapeutic feeding devices may be necessary to aid digestion and nutrition absorption.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and inflammatory conditions. Regular immunological assessments and consideration of prophylactic vaccinations are advised.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties. They may also display characteristics of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Management strategies involving physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and educational interventions are crucial.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (ear infections) and adenotonsillar hypertrophy (enlargement of the tonsils and adenoids), leading to difficulty breathing through the nose and possible sleep apnea. Regular ENT evaluations and management plans are essential.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision-related concerns include refractive errors (such as nearsightedness, farsightedness, and astigmatism), strabismus (eye misalignment), and presbyopia (difficulty focusing on close objects). Regular ophthalmologic examinations are recommended to monitor and address these issues.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome may develop skin conditions such as eczema, keratosis pilaris, and acne-like breakouts. Gentle skincare routines and avoiding harsh chemicals are key considerations.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Teeth abnormalities such as macrodontia (large permanent upper central incisors) and brachydactyly (shortened fingers) are common. Regular dental check-ups and orthodontic evaluation are necessary to address bite issues and maintain oral health.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Academic achievement can vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome. While many receive mainstream education, those with significant learning disabilities may require additional support in the classroom. Specialized educational programs and accommodations tailored to their unique needs are beneficial.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety, are frequent. Parental support groups and early intervention therapies can provide valuable assistance.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- The prevalence of behavioural traits suggests a genetic predisposition, potentially modifiable through targeted interventions and supportive environments.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal anomalies such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis) are common. Regular skeletal imaging (e.g., wrist X-rays) and monitoring for complications are advisable.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS

a) Screening:
- Regular dental check-ups and orthodontic evaluations.
- Ongoing monitoring for cardiovascular issues, particularly septal defects.
- Follow-up appointments for ENT concerns and periodic vision checks.

b) Treatments:
- Addressing feeding difficulties with specialized feeding tubes or devices.
- Managing respiratory infections with antibiotics and maintaining good hygiene practices.
- Considering surgical options for septal defects and cranial vault deformities.
- Implementing physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy programs.
- Providing educational supports and accommodations based on individual needs.
- Encouraging participation in parental support groups and online communities for emotional and practical guidance.

This comprehensive approach addresses the multifaceted challenges faced by individuals with KBG syndrome and their caregivers, ensuring holistic care and optimal outcomes.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent respiratory infections, including pneumonia and bronchiolitis.
  
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Common occurrence of respiratory tract infections, particularly in young children.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Presence of a ventricular septal defect (VSD).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Ventricular septal defects are commonly associated with KBG syndrome.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) and feeding issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) are common in KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Increased susceptibility to bacterial and viral infections.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Higher incidence of infectious diseases, especially in early childhood.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent seizures (epilepsy).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Epilepsy is a common feature in KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Nasal congestion and frequent sinus infections.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Upper respiratory tract infections are common and can lead to chronic sinusitis.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Glaucoma (increased intraocular pressure).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Glaucoma is a potential concern in KBG syndrome due to the presence of a VSD.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Hyperpigmentation of the skin.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Hyperpigmentation is a known dermatological feature in KBG syndrome.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Weak enamel leading to increased risk of tooth decay and sensitivity.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental issues, including weak enamel, are common in KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Need for additional educational support and accommodations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Additional educational support is often required for children with KBG syndrome.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral differences are a common feature in KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved 5th finger).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly and clinodactyly, are characteristic features of KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups.
- Monitoring for glaucoma (due to the VSD).
- Management of feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
- Consideration of behavioral therapies and educational supports.
- Regular cardiovascular assessments (e.g., echocardiogram, ECG) post-diagnosis.
- Monitoring for sensorineural hearing loss and conductive hearing loss.
- Regular orthodontic evaluations.
- Consideration of periodic cranial MRI scans for surveillance of brain structures.
- Regular ophthalmologic evaluations for vision-related concerns.
- Follow-up care for the VSD, including possible surgical intervention.
- Consideration of psychological support and interventions for behavioral differences.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary blockage of the Eustachian tubes (glue ear). These can lead to temporary hearing loss and difficulty breathing during colds or allergies.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat) review for any concerns.
  - Addressing potential allergic triggers and managing otitis media with tympanostomy tubes (grommets) as needed.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, particularly valve abnormalities and septal defects (holes between the heart chambers). These can result in various symptoms, including poor exercise tolerance, fatigue, and persistent cough.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular echocardiogram review for any concerns.
  - Follow-up with a pediatric cardiologist for further evaluation and management based on the specific heart defect(s).

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties, including refusal to breastfeed or bottle feed, regurgitation, and aspiration pneumonia. They may also develop gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and chronic constipation.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Consultation with a pediatric gastroenterologist for dietary and feeding strategies.
  - Consider referral for motility assessment and treatment if GERD or constipation is problematic.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, including Type 1 diabetes, thyroid disorders, and autoimmune hemolytic anemia. They may also have a higher incidence of autoimmune reactions to vaccines.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular immunological assessments and consideration of vaccine protocols accordingly.
  - Monitoring for autoimmune manifestations and initiating appropriate therapies if identified.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently demonstrate developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties. They may exhibit autistic-like behaviors, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Early intervention programs focusing on physical, occupational, and speech therapy.
  - Education and behavior management plans tailored to the child’s needs.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (ear infections) and glue ear (build-up of fluid in the ear), leading to temporary hearing loss and difficulty breathing during colds or allergies.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT review for any concerns.
  - Addressing potential allergens and managing otitis media with tympanostomy tubes (grommets) as needed.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of vision-related issues, including short-sightedness (hypermetropia), astigmatism, and refractive errors. They may also experience dry eyes and sensitivity to light.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ophthalmology review for any concerns.
  - Use of artificial tears and occlusion of the tear ducts (dacryocystorhinostomy) as indicated.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may have a predisposition to skin conditions, including eczema and keratosis pilaris (“goosebumps”). They may also experience delayed wound healing and pigmentation issues.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular dermatological review for any concerns.
  - Emollients and topical corticosteroids as necessary.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of tooth decay (dental caries) and bruxism (teeth grinding). They may also experience delayed eruption of adult teeth and supernumerary teeth (extra teeth).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Dental hygiene program focused on plaque control and fluoride application.
  - Regular orthodontic review for impacted teeth and possible extraction of supernumerary teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome typically require additional educational support, including Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and Speech-Language Therapy (SLT) evaluations. They may attend a special school or remain in mainstream education with accommodations and supports.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Implementation of an Individualized Education Program (IEP) outlining specific educational goals and interventions.
  - Provision of Speech-Language Therapy (SLT) services as deemed necessary.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently display behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety. They may struggle with social interactions and repetitive behaviors.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Introduction of targeted behavioral and educational interventions.
  - Parental support groups and counseling for emotional regulation.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience skeletal anomalies, including short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th finger (clinodactyly), and an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis). They may also have delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle (soft spot on the head) and hip dysplasia (dislocation of the hip joint).
- Management Recommendations:

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary blockage of the Eustachian tubes (glue ear). These can lead to hearing problems and difficulty breathing during colds or allergies.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT (ear, nose, throat) reviews for hearing concerns.
  - Monitoring for recurrent otitis media and glue ear.
  - Ensuring proper hydration and avoiding exposure to smoke or allergens.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at risk of congenital heart defects, particularly valve abnormalities and holes in the heart chambers (atrial septal defect and ventricular septal defect).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular cardiac reviews post-diagnosis.
  - Follow-up imaging (e.g., echocardiogram) as recommended by the treating cardiologist.
  - Consider referral for additional diagnostic testing or surgical intervention based on the presenting cardiac concerns.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), leading to poor weight gain and failure to thrive.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Consulting a pediatric gastroenterologist for dietary and feeding strategies.
  - Implementing a gradual introduction of solid foods and ensuring adequate hydration.
  - Treating GERD with antacids or proton pump inhibitors as per the treating physician’s guidance.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, particularly Type 1 diabetes mellitus and thyroid autoimmunity.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular screening for autoimmune markers and potential diagnoses.
  - Following immunological guidelines for autoimmune conditions.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- None noted.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- None noted.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Around 38% of patients with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve abnormalities, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Follow-up echocardiograms and EKGs are recommended annually post-diagnosis.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties, vomiting, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and constipation. They may also develop vitamin deficiencies due to poor absorption and potential malabsorption syndromes. Management includes dietary modifications, probiotics, and possible supplementation with vitamins B12, C, D, K, and iron.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, particularly Type 1 diabetes mellitus, thyroid autoimmunity, and inflammatory bowel disease. Regular screening for autoimmune markers and consideration of prophylactic immunomodulatory therapies are advised.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Neurodevelopmental outcomes in individuals with KBG syndrome are highly variable. While most exhibit mild-to-moderate delays in key developmental milestones, some demonstrate significant cognitive impairments requiring educational support. Behavioral differences, including autism spectrum traits, ADHD, and anxiety, are also commonly reported. Management strategies include early intervention programs, educational supports, behavioral interventions, and pharmacological treatments as indicated.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- KBG syndrome is associated with conductive hearing loss, which can lead to difficulty in amplifying sound and understanding speech. Audiometric evaluations and hearing aid utilization should be considered based on audiogram results.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision-related concerns in KBG syndrome include refractive errors (e.g., myopia, hypermetropia), astigmatism, and ocular motility issues. Regular ophthalmologic examinations are essential to monitor and address these concerns.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit skin pigmentation variations, eczema-like lesions, and hyperpigmented macules. Routine dermatologic assessments are advisable to monitor for and manage these manifestations.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Teeth characteristics, such as macrodontia (large permanent upper central incisors), brachydactyly (shortened fingers), and clinodactyly (curved fifth digit), are frequent among individuals with KBG syndrome. Dental care protocols should incorporate considerations for these anatomical features.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Academic achievement in children with KBG syndrome varies widely. Most receive educational support, including Individual Education Plans (IEPs) and accommodations, yet some require specialized placements or continued support beyond traditional schooling environments. Transition planning and ongoing assessment of academic needs are crucial components of managing educational outcomes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum traits, ADHD, and anxiety, are commonly reported. Speech delay and feeding challenges contribute to communication barriers and social interaction deficits.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Reports indicate variability in the prevalence of autism spectrum traits, ADHD, and anxiety in KBG syndrome populations. Early identification and targeted interventions play a critical role in supporting these neurodevelopmental factors.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal features, including brachydactyly (shortened fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth digit), are consistent observations in individuals with KBG syndrome. Monitoring for additional skeletal anomalies via X-rays and considering orthopedic referrals as warranted.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups.
- Regular hearing reviews to age 5 (if previous reviews provide a clear response).
- Eyesight (ophthalmology) review.
- Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).
- Referral for a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
- Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
- Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and behavioural therapy.

This comprehensive approach ensures that the unique medical needs of individuals with KBG syndrome are addressed, providing tailored guidance for future management and treatment options.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- None noted.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, such as recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary enlargement of the tonsils (tonsillar hypertrophy), which can lead to breathing difficulties and sleep apnea (pauses in breathing during sleep).

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- The presence of a septal defect (an opening in the wall separating the two upper chambers of the heart) requires ongoing monitoring and potential treatment options.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Septal defects are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome and can necessitate follow-up with a pediatric cardiologist and consideration of interventions such as closed septostomy tubes or surgical repair depending on the size and impact on heart function.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- The inability to chew and digest tougher foods increases the risk of choking and aspiration pneumonia, requiring careful dietary management.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome may have difficulty chewing and swallowing, increasing the risk of aspiration pneumonia and choking.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Immunological challenges, such as frequent bacterial and viral infections, highlight the importance of maintaining excellent hygiene practices and considering vaccinations appropriately.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Episodes of staring spells (cataplexy) can be concerning and disruptive, affecting play and social interactions.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Cataplexy is a recognized feature of KBG syndrome and can be triggered by emotions, physical exertion, or certain medications. Management strategies may include avoiding triggers, adjusting medication dosages, and exploring alternative therapies.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Frequent ear infections (otitis media) increase the likelihood of hearing loss and sleep disturbances due to disrupted breathing patterns (sleep apnea).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Otitis media is a common complication in KBG syndrome, leading to hearing loss and sleep disruption.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Vision-related issues, such as refractive errors (nearsightedness, farsightedness, astigmatism) and possible congenital cataracts, warrant regular ophthalmologic evaluations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision impairments, particularly refractive errors and congenital cataracts, are common in KBG syndrome and require periodic monitoring and corrective measures.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Difficulty chewing hard foods increases the risk of tooth decay and cavities.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental issues, including difficulty chewing and the need for orthodontic intervention, are common in KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Academic performance may vary based on the severity of learning difficulties and behavioral differences.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Academic achievement can vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, influenced by factors such as cognitive abilities, behavioral differences, and educational needs.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety, influence social interaction and routine behaviors.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral characteristics, including ASD, ADHD, and anxiety, can impact social behavior, routine activities, and overall functioning.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger) contribute to physical development and dexterity.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Physical features, including brachydactyly and clinodactyly, can influence hand-eye coordination, fine motor skills, and participation in sports or hobbies requiring precise movements.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
### Screening Recommendations:
- Regular dental check-ups: Monitoring for and treating dental issues, including the need for orthodontic intervention.
- Periodic vision assessments: Addressing refractive errors and preventing complications like amblyopia (lazy eye) and strabismus (eye misalignment).

### Treatments Recommendations:
- Speech therapy: To address delays in speech development and improve communication.
- Occupational therapy: To enhance fine motor skills and assist with self-care tasks.
- Behavioural therapy: To address behavioral differences and promote emotional regulation.
- Orthodontics: Considering braces or other orthopedic devices to correct jaw alignment issues.
- Anticonvulsants: For managing seizure activity, particularly if antiepileptic drugs are effective.
- Growth hormone: For promoting normal growth rates, particularly in children with slow growth velocities.
- Vestibular rehabilitation: To address balance and coordination issues, potentially improving gait and reducing falls.
- Audiologic evaluation: To rule out or treat hearing loss, which can exacerbate learning difficulties and behavioral differences.
- Cardiologist follow-up: Regular monitoring and management of heart conditions, including the septal defect and potential valve abnormalities.
- Neurodevelopmental assessment: Routine screening for cognitive, behavioral, and developmental delays, providing early identification and targeted interventions.

This comprehensive approach addresses the multifaceted challenges faced by individuals with KBG syndrome, ensuring a holistic and supportive care plan tailored to the unique needs of each patient.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (middle ear infections) and temporary enlargement of the tonsils (tonsillitis).

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of congenital heart defects, specifically abnormalities of the aortic valve and the pulmonary artery. These can lead to various heart-related issues, including persistent cyanotic heart disease requiring surgical intervention.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), leading to poor weight gain and delayed milestones.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases, particularly inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and type 1 diabetes mellitus.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties. They may also display autistic-like behaviors and experiences of seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to recurrent otitis media (ear infections) and adenotonsillar hypertrophy (enlargement of the lymph nodes in the throat), which can contribute to sleep apnea and breathing difficulties during sleep.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of vision problems, including short-sightedness (hypermetropia), astigmatism, and refractive errors. Regular eye checks are essential to monitor and address these issues.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome may develop skin tags (nevus comedonicum) and freckles (nevi) on the palms, soles, and scalp. Frequent hand washing can exacerbate this condition.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to tooth decay (dental caries) and gum disease (periodontal disease) due to their unique facial profile and susceptibility to bottle teething.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Education outcomes for individuals with KBG syndrome vary widely. While many achieve success in mainstream education, those with significant learning difficulties may require additional support and accommodations.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), anxiety, and challenges with social interaction, are common among individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently experience skeletal anomalies, such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), which can impact physical function and appearance.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
### Screening Recommendations:
- Regular dental check-ups starting from an early age.
- Monitoring for sensorineural hearing loss and ensuring timely referrals for audiologic evaluations.
- Periodic ophthalmological assessments to monitor for vision issues and correctable refractive errors.
- Routine ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat) examinations to rule out chronic sinusitis and evaluate for potential complications from enlarged tonsils.

### Treatments Recommendations:
- Management of GERD through dietary modifications, antacid medications, and, in severe cases, surgical interventions.
- Addressing feeding difficulties through specialized feeding programs and possibly orthodontic appliances.
- Managing seizures with appropriate anticonvulsant medication.
- Considering orthopedic evaluation for suspected brachydactyly and clinodactyly.
- Review and consideration of vestibular rehabilitation therapy for individuals experiencing balance or coordination issues.
- Evaluation and treatment of sleep apnea, potentially involving positional therapies or CPAP (Continuous Positive Airway Pressure) devices.
- Management of cognitive and behavioral differences through targeted educational strategies, behavior modification techniques, and psychological support.
- Monitoring and managing hormonal imbalances, such as thyroid dysfunction, through appropriate diagnostic testing and pharmacotherapy.
- Regular cardiovascular assessment, including echocardiography and EKG, to monitor for potential heart-related issues.
- Surveillance for autoimmune manifestations, such as IBD and type 1 diabetes, through periodic laboratory evaluations and immunological assessments.
- Periodic neurodevelopmental evaluations to track progress and identify areas for further intervention.
- Ongoing management of gastrointestinal issues, including dietary adjustments and possible enzyme replacement therapy for malabsorption syndromes.
- Regular review of hearing thresholds and considerations for hearing aid fitting, especially in those with recurrent otitis media.
- Monitoring for and addressing feeding difficulties through a multidisciplinary approach, including speech therapy, occupational therapy, and nutritional counseling.
- Periodic cranial MRI scans to assess for potential brain anomalies, particularly in infants and young children.
- Consideration of pacemaker placement for individuals with congenital heart defects requiring electrical pacing.
- Regular review of kidney function through appropriate laboratory assessments and monitoring for potential electrolyte imbalances.
- Periodic gastroenterological evaluations to address ongoing digestive concerns, including the need for repeat biopsies or endoscopic procedures.
- Consideration of vaccinations based on individual health status and the presence of underlying conditions that may predispose them to vaccine reactions or complications.

The recommendations offer practical guidance tailored to the unique needs of individuals with KBG syndrome, emphasizing the importance of ongoing monitoring, screening, and personalized care.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media and temporary nasal blockages, which can lead to breathing difficulties and infections.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat) review.
  - Addressing potential nasal blockages with saline sprays or irrigations.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at risk of congenital heart defects, particularly valve abnormalities.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular echocardiograms and ECGs to monitor heart health.
  - Follow-up care with a pediatric cardiologist as recommended.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), leading to vomiting and aspiration pneumonia.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Consulting with a pediatric gastroenterologist for dietary and feeding strategies.
  - Managing GERD with medications and dietary modifications.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are susceptible to autoimmune diseases and inflammatory conditions.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Monitoring for autoimmune manifestations.
  - Considering immunomodulatory therapies if autoimmune issues develop.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may exhibit developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Working with a multidisciplinary team including neurologists, psychologists, and educators.
  - Implementing strategies to address learning and behavior challenges.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to otitis media, which can lead to hearing loss and temporary nasal blockages.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Addressing potential nasal blockages with saline sprays or irrigations.
  - Ensuring proper hygiene practices to prevent infections.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at risk of vision-related issues, including refractive errors and strabismus.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular eye checks to monitor vision and address any concerns promptly.
  - Referral for orthoptic assessment if strabismus is noted.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may display a distinctive facial appearance characterized by a triangular-shaped face, wide-set eyes, and thick eyebrows.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Routine dermatological assessments to monitor skin conditions and address any concerns.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of developing tooth decay due to their feeding habits and anatomical features.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular dental check-ups and thorough cleaning routines.
  - Addressing feeding habits that contribute to tooth decay.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Educationally, children with KBG syndrome may require additional support in the classroom, requiring Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) or Special Educational Needs (SEN) plans.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Providing tailored educational programs and accommodations.
  - Collaborating with teachers, therapists, and specialists to create an inclusive learning environment.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioural and developmental differences are commonly observed in children with KBG syndrome, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Implementing therapeutic interventions such as Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Sensory Integration Therapy (SET).
  - Utilizing Early Start Denver System (ESDS) for infants and toddlers with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular X-rays and bone age assessments to monitor skeletal maturity.
  - Addressing brachydactyly with orthopedic intervention as necessary.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
### Screening:
- Regular dental check-ups.
- Monitoring for sensorineural hearing loss.
- Addressing feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

### Treatments:
- Speech therapy.
- Occupational therapy.
- Physical therapy.
- Behavioral therapy.
- Nutritional counseling.
- Anticonvulsants for seizure management.
- Antibiotics for recurrent otitis media.
- Hormone replacement therapy for growth hormone deficiency.
- Immunotherapy for autoimmune conditions.
- Orthodontic evaluation for craniofacial discrepancies.

This comprehensive approach ensures that the unique needs of each patient are addressed, providing targeted interventions and ongoing support throughout their lifetime.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son has mentioned struggling to see the board at school, especially when the teacher writes in small letters or from a distance. We've noticed this issue for a while now, and it seems to affect his ability to follow lessons comfortably. He often squints or leans forward to get a better view.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: There are times when our child doesn't respond immediately when called. It's as if he didn't hear us, even when we're standing right next to him. This has happened both at home and in quieter environments, so we're concerned it might be related to his hearing.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth seem to break or chip very easily. Even minor accidents, like biting into something hard or a slight knock against another tooth, can cause damage. We've had to take him to the dentist more frequently than usual because of this issue.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, our child was born with a septal defect. We've been working closely with cardiologists to monitor the condition and ensure it doesn't worsen over time. So far, the treatments and lifestyle adjustments have helped manage the issue effectively.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Our child gets tired quickly during physical activity. Simple tasks like playing outside or running around with friends can leave him exhausted sooner than his peers. This has been noticeable since he started engaging in more active play.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Our child has a feeding aversion. Certain textures or smells of food can put him off completely. Mealtime can be challenging, and we've had to work with him to find foods he's comfortable eating.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: In addition to the issues already mentioned, our child seems behind other children in development. His fontanelle also took longer to close than typical, which was another concern we've been monitoring. These developmental delays and physical differences have required us to adapt his education and activities to better suit his needs.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: To be honest, I'm a bit overwhelmed with all her appointments and tests... Um, she does rub her eyes a lot, especially when she's trying to focus on something. I'm not sure if it's just a habit or something more, but it worries me.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Oh dear, I think she can hear some things but not others. It's like she tunes out certain sounds or voices. I've noticed it's harder for her to understand me when there's background noise. I'm not sure if she needs help with this or if it's just my imagination.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Yes... her teeth. She complains about sensitivity, especially with cold foods like ice cream or frozen yogurt. It's been a real issue since she started eating solid foods. I'm hoping it's just a phase, but it's been going on for a while now.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist said we need to keep an eye on her heart because of some concerns they found. We go back for regular check-ups to make sure everything is okay. That's all I know, to be frank.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: She seems a bit clumsy compared to other kids her age. Like, the other day she tripped over her own feet. And her coordination could be better. The specialist mentioned keeping an eye on this.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding was a nightmare when she was little. She would spit up a lot and had trouble latching on. But that seems to have passed now. 

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Honestly, I feel like I'm forgetting something... Oh yes, the developmental pediatrician said she seems behind where she should be for her age. They want us to work on some things at home to help catch her up. That's about it, I think. Sorry, I'm just really worried about her and want to make sure we're doing everything we can.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media (ear infections) and potential for chronic lung issues.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat) review.
  - Antibiotics for recurrent otitis media.
  - Monitoring for potential chronic lung issues.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at risk of congenital heart defects, specifically a hole in the heart (atrial septal defect) and ventricular septal defect.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Cardiac review following diagnosis.
  - Follow-up echocardiogram and ECG as per clinical judgment.
  - Consider MRI of the chest (tethered cord) if sacral dimple is noted.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Work with feeding specialists and dietary requirements.
  - Address GERD with antacid medications and dietary modifications.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of developing autoimmune diseases, particularly Type 1 diabetes and inflammatory bowel disease.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular screening for autoimmune conditions.
  - Immunotherapy options under consideration.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience developmental delays, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Physiotherapy and occupational therapy as indicated.
  - Speech therapy as indicated.
  - Behavioral therapy as indicated.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to otitis media (middle ear infections) and adenotonsillar hypertrophy (enlargement of the tonsils and adenoids).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular ENT review.
  - Antibiotics for recurrent otitis media.
  - Consider tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy as indicated.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of vision-related issues, including refractive errors (hypermetropia/hyperopia) and strabismus (eye misalignment).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular eye checks.
  - Orthoptic assessment as indicated.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may exhibit a distinctive facial appearance characterized by a triangular-shaped face, wide-set eyes, and thick eyebrows that sometimes fuse together (synophrys).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular dermatological review as indicated.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of tooth decay (dental caries) and orthodontic concerns due to brachydactyly (shortened fingers).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Early dental intervention.
  - Orthodontic evaluation as indicated.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Education outcomes for children with KBG syndrome vary widely. Many benefit from additional support and accommodations in the classroom, while others transition to mainstream education.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Provision of an Individualized Education Plan (IEP) as appropriate.
  - Support services such as Speech Therapy, Occupational Therapy, and Physical Therapy.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety, are commonly observed in children with KBG syndrome.
- Management Recommendations:
  - Consultation with a pediatric neurologist or psychiatrist for appropriate referrals.
  - Implementation of behavior management strategies as indicated.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at increased risk of skeletal abnormalities, including brachydactyly (shortened fingers) and an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
- Management Recommendations:
  - Regular skeletal review (X-rays of wrist, hip, spine, and skull).
  - Observation of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigation as indicated.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
### Screening:
- Regular ENT review.
- Regular eye checkups.
- Periodic cardiac review (echo and ECG).

### Treatments:
- Anticonvulsants for seizure management.
- Antibiotics for recurrent otitis media.
- Speech therapy as indicated.
- Orthodontic evaluation for brachydactyly.
- Behavioral therapy as indicated.
- Consider tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy for enlarged tonsils and adenoids.

This completes the clinical report following the specified 13-category schema layout.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome may experience respiratory issues, including recurrent otitis media and potential for chronic lung disease due to incomplete closure of the airways (tracheoesophageal fistula).

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at risk of congenital heart defects, specifically a condition known as tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF), which can lead to breathing difficulties and feeding issues.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), which can contribute to aspiration pneumonia and other digestive issues.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to infections due to their immune system being compromised, potentially leading to frequent illnesses requiring hospitalization.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Neurological features in KBG syndrome include developmental delays, behavioral differences, and seizures. Learning disabilities and autistic-like behaviors are also common.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are prone to otitis media (middle ear infections), which can lead to hearing loss and temporary or permanent deafness.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision-related concerns in KBG syndrome include refractive errors (such as nearsightedness, farsightedness, and astigmatism), strabismus (eye misalignment), and possible treatment-resistant vision problems.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit eczema, skin tags, and other dermatological abnormalities.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Dental issues in KBG syndrome include weak enamel, susceptibility to tooth decay, and orthodontic concerns such as bruxism (teeth grinding) and malocclusion (misaligned teeth).

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Academic achievement in children with KBG syndrome can vary widely. While many receive mainstream education, those with significant learning challenges may require additional support and accommodations.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioral and developmental differences are common in KBG syndrome, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety. Management strategies may include behavior therapy, educational interventions, and social skills training.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Skeletal features in KBG syndrome include brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved fifth finger), along with a unique shoulder blade shape (pseudo-tetragon). These can impact posture and athletic performance.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
### Screening Recommendations:
- Regular dental check-ups starting soon after diagnosis.
- Monitoring for sensorineural hearing loss and referring for audiological assessment if concerns arise.
- Periodic ophthalmology evaluations to address vision needs and prevent complications from refractive errors.
- Considering early intervention for suspected neurodevelopmental delays and behavioral differences.

### Treatments Recommendations:
- Addressing feeding difficulties with dietary modifications and possibly nasogastric tube feeding.
- Managing otitis media with antibiotics and considering surgical options for impacted adenoids.
- Treating seizures with anticonvulsants as per medical guidance.
- Managing gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) with dietary adjustments and medications.
- Providing orthopedic evaluation for brachydactyly and clinodactyly.
- Conducting periodic cardiovascular assessments, especially in young children.
- Reviewing and managing the need for orthodontic interventions for malocclusions.
- Implementing behavioral therapies and educational supports tailored to individual needs.
- Encouraging participation in physical activities under adult supervision, ensuring safety precautions are taken.
- Monitoring for and treating sleep apnea, which can exacerbate existing health issues.
- Evaluating the need for psychological support and interventions based on the presence of behavioral differences.
- Considering genetic counseling for siblings and future pregnancies, given the high likelihood of recurrence in families with a history of KBG syndrome.
